bullets.title: INTC: $15B Follow-On Offering Priced Monday, Stock -3.6% Pre-Market
bullets.body: Intel launched a $15B primary common stock offering (plus 15% greenshoe) with JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup as bookrunners, pricing post-close Monday Aug 10. Proceeds earmarked for capex and working capital. Stock dropped ~3.6% in pre-market on dilution concerns at ~$101.65/share.

bullets.title: AAPL: Jefferies Downgrades to Sell; All-Glass iPhone Canceled, CXMT Memory Tests Flagged
bullets.body: Jefferies cut AAPL to Underperform (from Hold) and lowered PT to $263.66 (from $285.56), citing cancellation of the all-glass iPhone due to low glass midframe yields — a major setback for the $2,060 blended ASP strategy. Apple is separately testing Chinese CXMT memory chips across iPhones and MacBooks to offset supply squeeze, with White House approval being sought for China-market devices. iPhone 18 Pro unit costs expected up ~40%, pressuring margins.

bullets.title: TTD: Double-Downgrade Day — DA Davidson to Neutral ($16 PT), HSBC to Reduce ($10 PT)
bullets.body: Trade Desk was hit by two downgrades following Q2 results. DA Davidson cut to Neutral from Buy (PT $16 from $29) citing accelerating spend loss and minimal visibility. HSBC cut to Reduce from Hold (PT $10 from $20), implying 28% downside. FactSet consensus target sits at ~$14.39, range $9–$30; stock was trading ~$13.80.

bullets.title: META: +1.8–3% Pre-Market on Muse Glimmer AI Launch & Zuckerberg Open-Source Essay
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model optimized for on-device inference (single GPU), partnering with AMD, ARM, Dell, and NVDA. Zuckerberg published an essay positioning Meta as the US open-source AI leader vs. centralized competitors and outlined a vision for free/affordable superintelligence. Stock up 1.8–3% pre-market.

bullets.title: MU: UBS Raises PT to $1,625; HBM ASPs +79% Y/Y, DRAM Undersupplied Through 2Q28
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on MU with $1,625 PT, raising HBM blended ASP forecast to +79% Y/Y (from +67%) with HBM4E pricing expected to exceed $30/GB. DRAM expected undersupplied through at least Q2 2028; NAND pricing to peak in Q4 2027. UBS EPS estimates: $74 (2026), $185 (2027), $266 (2028) — well above consensus. NVDA de-specced VR300 to 384GB HBM4 (from 768GB HBM4E) due to supply tightness, further tightening available supply.

bullets.title: TTWO: Q1 Beats, GTA VI Nov 19 Launch Confirmed; Analysts Cluster at $285–$300
bullets.body: Take-Two beat Q1 net bookings by 2.2% and adj. EPS by 6.1%. GTA VI confirmed for Nov 19 release with an Aug 27 Netflix-exclusive trailer (6-hour window). Q2 bookings guided below consensus ($1.62–1.67B vs $1.75B), but FY27 guidance reaffirmed at $8.0–8.2B. Wolfe raised unit estimate to 40M (from 35M) at $85 blended ASP; PT $289. BMO at $285, B Riley/DA Davidson at $300. 90% buy-side.

bullets.title: NET: $2.175B Convertible Notes Offering Due 2031; Stock -2.1% Pre-Market
bullets.body: Cloudflare announced a private offering of $2.175B in convertible senior notes due 2031. Stock was at $300.27 at announcement and fell ~2.1% in pre-market. Q2 revenue of $696M (+36% YoY) beat consensus per separate security research note; SASE gaining share.

bullets.title: HPE: Morgan Stanley Upgrades to Overweight, PT $69 (~30% Upside)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded Hewlett Packard Enterprise to Overweight from Equal-Weight with a PT of $69 (down slightly from $71 prior), implying ~30% upside from $53.22. Upgrade driven by AI and 'chipflation' tailwinds to estimate revisions across IT Hardware. Stock +4.3% pre-market.

bullets.title: NVDA: $2–3B Investment in Lancium; Rubin De-Spec'd Due to HBM Supply Tightness
bullets.body: NVDA announced an investment of up to $3B in Stargate data center power developer Lancium (~$2B for ~20% stake). Separately, NVDA de-specced its VR300 chip to 384GB HBM4 (from 768GB HBM4E originally) due to HBM supply tightness per Citi semi checks. JPM notes Vera Rubin chips expected to monetize at $30–$50/watt.

bullets.title: AMD: Taalas Acquisition Broadens Custom Silicon Inference Stack
bullets.body: UBS notes AMD's Taalas acquisition enables hard-coded model weights into silicon fabric, eliminating weight fetches and reducing memory requirements vs. GPU/SRAM architectures — a competitive moat for high-volume inference. AMD Q2 described as 'somewhat disappointing' but sets up better year-end positioning with Meta/OpenAI ramps and TSMC 2nm tailwinds per Citi semis lunch notes.

bullets.title: TSM: July Revenue +45% Y/Y on AI Chip Demand; Capex Guidance Raised to $60–64B
bullets.body: TSMC reported approximately 45% July revenue growth year-over-year (to NT$467.58B) driven by continued AI chip demand. The company raised 2026 capex guidance to $60–64B and guided full-year sales growth above 40% in USD. Morgan Stanley recommends TSMC as a key Overweight in Greater China semis.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM Highlights Monster Q2 — 30%+ Growth, Remains on Analyst Focus List
bullets.body: Shopify delivered 30%+ growth in both revenue and gross profit in Q2, with Q3 guidance exceeding expectations across all metrics per JPM Internet comp sheet. JPM described it as a 'monster quarter' and retains SHOP on its Analyst Focus List. Stock was among top performers in JPM's internet coverage, +~29% on the week.

bullets.title: DASH & CART: Both Beat on Unit Economics; DASH +10%, CART +12% Post-Earnings
bullets.body: DoorDash gained ~10% post-earnings on a significant profit beat with improved unit economics across all segments. Instacart rose ~12% on a beat-and-raise despite competition concerns, and was also up ~2% in Monday pre-market. Both highlighted as strong performers in JPM's internet coverage recap.

bullets.title: FWONK: $600M Convertible Notes Offering for Capped Calls & 2027 Note Repayment
bullets.body: Liberty Media announced a $600M aggregate principal convertible senior notes private offering. Proceeds are earmarked to fund capped call transactions related to its 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027, plus working capital and repayment of those 2027 notes.

bullets.title: FOXA: Files Automatic Mixed Shelf (S-3ASR) of Indeterminate Amount
bullets.body: Fox Corp. filed an S-3ASR automatic mixed shelf registration statement for an unspecified amount of securities. Wolfe's Sunday note flagged FOXA as having standout risk/reward at ~6.5x EBITDA with healthy consensus beats.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: PSKY Offers 45-Day Exclusive Theatrical Windows + 30 Films/Year Guarantee
bullets.body: Palace Sky (PSKY) offered three-year theater exclusivity contracts guaranteeing 45-day exclusive theatrical windows and a 90-day no-streaming provision contingent on its WBD acquisition closing, plus a commitment to release 30 films annually in theaters. Wolfe maintains Underperform on PSKY despite management progress.

bullets.title: NFLX: GTA VI Exclusive Trailer Distribution a Growth Play With Model Risk — Wolfe
bullets.body: Netflix's agreement to host the GTA VI trailer with 6-hour exclusivity on Aug 27 signals the platform's ongoing effort to sustain double-digit subscriber/sales growth through gaming partnerships. Wolfe sees it as a growth play but flags business model limitations and notes NFLX bottomed at ~13x EPS.

bullets.title: CSCO: JPM Expects F4Q Beat but Cautions FY27 Guide May Disappoint; Reports Wed
bullets.body: JPM expects a comfortable F4Q26 beat (revenue $16.9–17.0B vs $16.8B consensus) driven by strong AI and non-AI momentum, but warns FY27 guidance may fall shy of elevated investor expectations. Stock trading at 25x+ NTM EPS, +60% YTD. Gross margin pressure expected from component cost inflation. Reports Wednesday after close.

bullets.title: RBLX: Weekly Engagement Flat W/W at 20M CCUs; Steep -22% Y/Y Comp Headwind
bullets.body: JPM's Roblox engagement tracker shows peak CCUs flat week-over-week at ~20M but down 22% Y/Y through the first 8 days of August, with August representing the toughest viral comp period (21.5M avg CCUs last year). No new viral hits identified; long-tail engagement remains healthy vs. pre-2025 baseline.

bullets.title: SNOW: Cortex AI Gateway Positions as Enterprise Agent Governance Layer; Bullish Read from GS
bullets.body: Snowflake launched Cortex AI Gateway (private preview) as a centralized governance control plane for AI models, agents, and MCP tools — competing directly with Databricks Unity AI Gateway. GS strategists are incrementally positive on SNOW, citing the Cortex Code ramp as an early positive. Observe on Iceberg feature could be a modest negative for DDOG and DT.
